title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-rajiv-patel
content:
Context:
- Working on reproducing intermittent OOMs in dedicated inference pool (g4dn-type nodes) while running batched generation for length-2048 requests.
- Happens more often on batches >= 8 with seq_len 1024+, but observed at batch=4 in heavy quantized runs.
- Kernel: torchvision/transform + LLM model (quantized 4-bit).

Observed errors / snippets (copied from node logs):
1) CUDA OOM: tried to allocate X GiB (GPU 0)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.50 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 12.30 GiB already allocated; 1.24 GiB free; 256.00 MiB cached)
  File "/workspace/model/serving.py", line 423, in generate
    out = model.generate(input_ids, max_length=... )

2) driver/library mismatch warnings right before OOM (system log):
[W drvr] Libcuda reported version 11.2 but driver reports 11.1 - possible incompatibility
NVRM: API mismatch: the client has the version 450.80.02, the kernel module has the version 450.66.00

3) cuDNN failure seen in one trace: 
CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED at /opt/conda/conda-bld/pytorch_159...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1190, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*input, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: cuDNN error: CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED

Commands I ran locally / on node to collect info:
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DRIVER,UTILIZATION
  -> driver: 450.80.02, GPU mem usage shows fragmentation (small free blocks)
- nvidia-smi topo -m
- nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo via pynvml to capture allocations before crash
- ps aux | grep python ; check process cmdline to confirm right container
- docker inspect <container> | jq .Config.Env to get CUDA env vars
- python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.backends.cudnn.version(), torch.__version__)'
  -> torch 1.11.0, cuda 11.3 (build), cudnn 8201
- ldconfig -p | grep cuda; ls -l /usr/local/cuda*
- ldd $(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.__file__)') | grep libcudnn

Hypotheses / notes:
- Mismatch between libcuda and kernel driver reported in syslog may cause non-deterministic failures in cuDNN kernels, but usually gives explicit driver mismatch errors.
- OOM could be exacerbated by fragmentation from persistent CUDA contexts and multiple model copies (we use model sharding across processes in container).
- Quantized kernels might allocate pinned host buffers or have different memory patterns (fragmentation + temporary workspace).
- PyTorch build CUDA vs system driver mismatch: if PyTorch expects a newer CUDA runtime than driver supports, some kernels might fall back or behave badly.

Immediate mitigations to try (quick):
- Reduce batch size to 4 or 2 in canary to see if crash disappears (already reduces frequency).
- torch.cuda.empty_cache() after heavy operations (but this is usually no-op for fragmentation).
- Set environment: PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 (test perf impact)
- Use max_split_size_mb to reduce fragmentation: torch.backends.cuda.max_split_size_mb = 128 (experiment).
- Switch off cudnn benchmark (torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False) to force deterministic algos with smaller workspace.
- Try single-process TF-style serving (no multiprocessing) to see if fragmentation from worker forks is the issue.

Longer-term / infra fixes to validate:
- Align driver / CUDA versions across AMIs: confirm driver 470.* for CUDA 11.4+ if we build PyTorch for 11.4. Consider baking driver into AMI and pin to model build.
- Build and deploy a small repro binary that allocates and frees large tensors repeatedly to reproduce fragmentation pattern.
- Upgrade to torch 1.12/1.13 build that matches system CUDA (or rebuild wheels against system CUDA).
- Add more robust OOM handling in serving stack (catch OOM, drop-in fallback to smaller batch or model variant, log full nvml snapshot).

Repro steps I used (approx):
1) Start container on dedicated node (g4dn.xlarge) with image: redwood/serving:canary-quant-2025-11
   docker run --gpus all -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -it --rm image /bin/bash
2) Inside container: conda activate rwinf; python -m uvicorn serving.app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
3) Send load via locust / wrk with payload: batch_size=8, seq_len=1024, temperature 0.8, top_p 0.95
4) Wait ~30-90s observe OOM in container logs and host dmesg shows driver mismatch logged earlier that lifetime.

Useful commands / snippets to collect if this happens again (add to incident script):
- nvprof / Nsight systems (heavy)
- sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i nvrm
- python -c "import pynvml; pynvml.nvmlInit(); h=pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0); print(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo(h));"
- collect ldd for pytorch: ldd $(python -c 'import torch as t; print(t.__file__)') | egrep 'cuda|cudnn|cublas'
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- journalctl -k -n 200 | grep NVRM

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is this only happening on g4dn or also on p3/p4p? Need to repro on multiple instance types.
- Confirm if AMI driver differs from host driver (we run container with host drivers; check host kernel module version vs container libcuda).
- Add a periodic memory defrag (restart worker) policy when fragmentation crosses threshold.
- Run a controlled experiment with deterministic memory alloc/free pattern to isolate fragmentation vs true capacity OOM.

Notes to self (short):
- If driver mismatch persists, escalate to infra to update node AMI and restart nodes.
- Keep an eye on any cuDNN execution failed traces — could be silent sign of kernel incompat.
- When changing batch size, also record latency tail to ensure perf regressions are acceptable.

Last test run summary (2026-02-20):
- Batch=8, seq_len=1024 -> OOM in 47s on node A (driver 450.80.02), fragmentation observed.
- Batch=4, seq_len=1024 -> no OOM in 10m stress test.
- After setting PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1, allocation pattern different but latency up ~12%. No OOM in 5m test (not conclusive).

If I get time next:
- Rebuild image with torch wheel matching system CUDA 11.1 or upgrade driver to 11.3+, run full stress.
- Add nvml snapshots to logs on OOM for postmortem (env var REDWOOD_DUMP_NVML_ON_OOM=1).

-- Rajiv
(quick hack notes, will tidy and move to confluence if we get a reliable repro)
